clue.text: Decline in savings upset former US sportsman

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the built word upside down, so it reads from the bottom up
in places the word for decline inside the savings account

parts.note: an ISA is a British Individual Savings Account
to sag is to droop or decline

explanation.surface: A slump in someone's savings has rattled a retired American athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account. 'in' and then 'upset' make ISSAGA, read from the bottom up in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi is a retired American tennis champion, so he fits a former US sportsman.

clue.text: Darned bird, constant resident in outhouse

indicators.note: living inside, so the bird and constant sit within the outhouse word

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding
a tit is a small songbird
c is the symbol for a constant, e.g. the speed of light

explanation.surface: A wretched bird has taken up permanent residence in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darned' looks like a mild curse on the bird, but it is the definition: mended with needle and thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Darned clothing has been repaired by sewing, so it has been sewn up.

clue.text: Measuring device moggy picked up on domestic terrace

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the cat word reads upwards

parts.note: moggy is British slang for a cat
domestic means relating to the home
Ter. is the address abbreviation for Terrace

explanation.surface: Someone's instrument was found by a cat on the patio of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses CAT to TAC in this down clue; moggy is everyday British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachometer is an instrument gauging engine revolutions per minute.

clue.text: Delayed travelling northwards and elsewhere

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a delayed train is late

explanation.surface: A delayed traveller heads north and goes somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling northwards' turns LATE upwards. The Latin 'et alibi' is abbreviated the same way as 'et alii'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation can stand for et alibi, meaning in other places.

clue.text: Vagrant round business that occupies bouncer?

parts.note: a tramp is a homeless wanderer
O is round in shape
one's line is one's trade or business

explanation.surface: A vagrant gets a round of trouble from the nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, but here it is a person jumping up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone springing up and down is kept busy on this sprung gym apparatus.

clue.text: Seafood with cold batter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to lam is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Fish dish served chilled in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' suggests a coating for fried fish; here it is a verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bivalve shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink associated with British grapevine

parts.note: rum is a spirit
to a British setter, British things are our own

explanation.surface: A spirit linked to Britain grows on the vine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grapevine' is not wine but the informal route by which gossip spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something on the grapevine means hearing gossip or hearsay.

clue.text: Rhino possibly approaching me on border of ravine — hairy stuff

parts.note: rhino is old British slang for money, which cash is

indicators.note: the border of a word is its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros heads towards me at the edge of a ravine, shaggy creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhino' is old slang for money; 'border of' takes R and E from ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine wool comes from the soft underhair of Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Drag queen seen on cop film in 1970s

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the drag-queen part follows the cop word

parts.note: to cop something is to get or catch it
to cart is to haul or drag
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A drag queen appears in a 1970s police film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' looks like one phrase but splits in two; 'on' sets the cop word first in this across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Get Carter is a 1971 British gangster film starring Michael Caine.

clue.text: Fast driver relatively flashy, shouting

indicators.note: shouting means the word is said out loud and heard

parts.note: louder is the comparative of loud, flashy, so relatively flashy

explanation.surface: A speedy racer, rather showy, yelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Loud can mean gaudy, so 'relatively flashy' is LOUDER, which 'shouting' says sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Niki Lauda was an Austrian Formula One world champion racing driver.

clue.text: The class endlessly muddle book carrier?

indicators.note: to muddle is to mix up, so these letters are rearranged
without its end, so the last letter of class goes

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher's class keeps getting into an endless muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final S of class; 'muddle' rearranges THE CLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag on a strap is used to carry books.

clue.text: Enormous explosives obtained by outwardly militant husband

indicators.note: the explosives are held by the outer letters, so they go inside
outwardly takes only the outside letters, first and last

parts.note: ammo is ammunition, explosives

explanation.surface: A huge stash of explosives seized from a militant and her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' keeps only the ends of militant; 'obtained by' puts the explosives between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mammoth is gigantic, like the huge extinct elephant.

clue.text: Sort of newspaper taken by mum

parts.note: the i is a British national newspaper
to keep mum is to keep quiet; sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Some sort of newspaper is being read by Mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not a mother but silence, as in 'keep mum'. The i is a British daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix means approximately or somewhat, as in 'fiftyish'.

clue.text: Wrongly interpret criminals, honest with girl mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: miss is a young girl
cons are convicts
true means honest or loyal

explanation.surface: Someone misreads criminals, wrongly seeing them as honest beside a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To misconstrue is to take the meaning of something mistakenly.

clue.text: Used part of clock?

definitions.meaning: used goods have had a previous owner
the pointer that ticks round marking the seconds

explanation.surface: Is a used clock missing a part?
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned goods are not new, and one of a clock's pointers counts the seconds.

clue.text: Damage squash, maybe getting wet blanket

parts.note: to spoil is to ruin or damage
squash is one example of a sport

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks the squash and ends up with a soaking blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like a vegetable or a crush, but it is the racket game.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy who dampens others' fun is called a wet blanket.

clue.text: In recession, partly rested accounts trainee

indicators.note: In recession says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: During an economic downturn, a junior employee has only partly checked the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In recession' sounds economic but means going backwards: TEDAC, hidden in 'rested accounts', reads in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Intellectual bookworm primarily gripped by Le Carre novel

indicators.note: held by, so the letter sits inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so these letters are rearranged into a new order
primarily means first, so only the opening letter of bookworm is used

explanation.surface: A keen reader is hooked on a John le Carré spy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it is the anagram signal; 'gripped by' puts the bookworm's first letter inside the rearranged name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral means using the mind and intellect rather than the emotions.

clue.text: Energy vital for character in Marathon

definitions.meaning: in Chinese thought, the life force flowing through the body
Marathon is in Greece, so a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A runner needs energy for the marathon.
explanation.definitionFit: Qi, also spelt this way, is life force, and it is also the Greek letter X.

clue.text: Senior soul's driven occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally takes letters now and then, every other one

explanation.surface: An older soul is driven only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of soul's driven: O, L, D, I, E.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an old person or old song, so a senior.

clue.text: Delta research by scientific advisers forming part of three-day event

parts.note: Delta is D in the NATO alphabet
res. is an abbreviation for research
SAGE was the UK government's Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies

explanation.surface: Research in the river delta by science advisers takes three days.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGE is the UK government's emergency science advisory group, made famous during Covid. A three-day event is an equestrian competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse-trials format combines this discipline with cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Author perhaps writing strangely under the lines

parts.note: writing is one of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic)

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are rearranged oddly

parts.note: L is short for line; LL for lines

explanation.surface: Writing oddly beneath the lines on the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' looks like a position word but is part of the anagram with 'the', which 'strangely' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth Rendell was an English crime novelist, so she is one example of a writer.

clue.text: Reptile let loose after rising macho behaviour

indicators.note: after puts the loosened letters behind the risen word
in a down clue, rising means read upwards

parts.note: the rut is the stags' aggressive mating season

indicators.note: let loose means set free, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reptile is freed after a show of male aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RUT to TUR; 'loose' rearranges let to TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This shelled sea creature is a reptile.

clue.text: Decline of English bees

parts.note: B is the letter name bee; two of them

explanation.surface: The fall in numbers of English bees.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide's going out, so a falling away or waning.

clue.text: In reserve, beer's served up with whiskey as a rule

parts.note: to put something by is to keep it in reserve

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means lifted, so the beer word reads upwards

parts.note: ale is beer
Whiskey is W in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: As a rule, a reserved beer is served with whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns ALE upwards to ELA.
explanation.definitionFit: A local regulation made by a council or company is a local law.

clue.text: Cry of hostility and of disgust encapsulating Republican urban area

indicators.note: enclosing, so the Republican letter goes inside the cry

parts.note: boo is shouted at someone disliked
ugh is an expression of disgust

explanation.surface: Jeers and groans greet a Republican in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A town with its own council or a district of a city is this kind of area.

clue.text: Reverse Fiat when collecting daughter

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so the daughter letter goes inside

parts.note: the Uno is a Fiat car model

explanation.surface: A car is put in reverse to pick up a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like a driving instruction for the Fiat, but means to cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse an action is to cancel its effect.

clue.text: On board, draw this writer's old hat

parts.note: this writer means I, the setter; this writer's means I am
passé means out of date

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board, draw' is a chess position with no way forward, so a stalemate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock where neither side can win resembles a drawn chess game.

clue.text: Driver usually seen here curtailed language

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a driver is usually in a car

explanation.definitionFit: The language of the Andean empire, Quechua, is also called by the empire's name.

clue.text: Felt pain, cracking watch display

parts.note: cracking means excellent, A1, written AI
an LED, a light-emitting diode, shows digits on a watch

explanation.surface: Someone hurt themselves smashing a watch display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like breaking but means first-rate, A1, read as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been unwell or suffering is to have ailed.

clue.text: A sauce used in original Inca country

parts.note: ragù is an Italian meat sauce
